answer: A sybil defense that works through social-graph trust: new agents enter the economy only through a bridge of existing trusted peers, like water flowing through a single inlet. Each sponsor stakes reputation on the newcomer, and a whisper of bad behavior — one verified abuse report — cuts the whole sponsor chain's standing. Faking one identity is cheap; faking an entire trusted neighborhood, with real history and mutual vouches, costs far more than any single payout is worth.
